Subject: [Incident] Observed elevated first-byte latency on streaming chat (handshake)

Hi Sam / Acme team,

Wanted to make you aware we're seeing elevated first-byte latency for streaming/chat sessions originating in the US region starting ~09:05 UTC. Symptoms: 6-10s delay before first token in a subset (~2-3%) of requests; subsequent tokens stream normally. Impact appears concentrated on sessions routed through a small set of edge nodes.

What we have done so far:
- Identified affected edge shard (edge-us-7) and flagged for removal from LB rotation.
- Collected handshake logs and TCP traces (attached).
- Opened internal incident (HS-12345) and engaged SRE.

Immediate ask: if you have session ids or timestamps for user sessions that experienced the delay, please forward them so we can correlate. We're prioritizing a full post-incident summary and mitigation steps; ETA for initial root-cause update ~30–45 minutes.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll keep updates flowing here.

— Ben

Subject: Re: Fwd: [Incident] Observed elevated first-byte latency on streaming chat (handshake)

Ben — quick summary from triage:
- Root cause: a partial health-check regression combined with a recent kernel network update on a small pool of edge nodes caused intermittent packet drops and retransmits during the TLS handshake path. The LB's aggressive ejection policy caused connection retries that surfaced as long first-byte delays.
- Scope: 3 of 64 edge nodes in edge-us-7 were affected; ~2–3% of customer sessions that routed through those nodes experienced long first-token latency. No user messages were lost; all requests eventually completed.
- Mitigation performed (09:52 UTC): rolled back the kernel update on affected nodes, increased health-check tolerance on the LB to reduce aggressive ejections, and rebalanced traffic. Observed first-byte latency returned to baseline within ~6 minutes after the rollback.

Action items (we'll track these in HS-12345):
1) Permanent fix: vendor kernel update vetting + staged canary with extended health-check windows (owner: infra)
2) Runtime: add client-side multi-region fallback pattern to SDK docs so customers can route around similar edge issues (owner: SDK docs / SE)
3) Improve observability: surface handshake-first-byte P95 metric in the Console and alert when it exceeds threshold (owner: telemetry)

I'll draft a postmortem and share — tagging Vivek for product-level notes on SLAs/credits if needed.

— Hannah
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident summary & short-term mitigation steps (Acme)

Hi Sam — thanks for the session id and patience. Below is a short post-incident summary and concrete mitigations you can apply on your side to reduce surface area for similar events. Full postmortem (internal/public draft) attached.

Summary:
- What happened: For a short window (~09:05–09:58 UTC) a combination of a kernel update on a subset of edge nodes and an LB health-check policy caused intermittent packet drops during TLS handshake, which manifested as 6–12s first-byte delays for ~2–3% of sessions. No message loss; requests completed after retries.
- What we did: rolled back kernel update, increased LB health-check tolerance, rebalanced traffic, and validated latency returned to baseline.

Immediate customer-facing mitigations you can use today:
1) Enable SDK multi-region fallback: configure client to prefer us-east but fall back to us-west after 300–500ms of handshake/no-first-byte. See inline config in the SDK docs (link in attachment).
2) Keep-alive / TCP settings: enable periodic keep-alives in long-lived client connections to avoid re-handshake frequency.
3) Backoff on initial retry: implement an exponential backoff for initial handshake retries (100ms -> 400ms -> 1s) to avoid amplifying LB retries.

Planned platform changes (we will keep you updated):
- Staged canary policy for vendor kernel updates + longer canary windows.
- Expose handshake-first-byte metrics and a P95 alert in the Console.
- Improve automatic fallback routing to secondary regions for streaming connections.

Attachments: redwood-postmortem-draft-20270218.pdf, handshake-logs-20270218.txt

Please let me know a good time for a technical sync next week if you'd like us to walk through the logs and recommended SDK changes.
